sheets.title: Settings › Security › Formats — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: The panel's header keys, read from the browser. Before, three: export the native manifest, the vault SOPS sheet, age armor. There was no way to open a SOPS *document* at all — the SOPS row claimed read, write and 'this browser' while offering no road to a file. After, four: the same three plus `SOPS document`, which is the road. The row's claim and what the panel can do now agree.
sheets.before: header keys: Export native protection manifest, Vault SOPS, age armor (3)
sheets.after: header keys: Export native protection manifest, SOPS document, Vault SOPS, age armor (4)

sheets.title: The SOPS document sheet — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: Before is the same panel again, because pressing `SOPS document` did nothing: the key did not exist, so the capture has nothing to open. After is the sheet — choose a file, an age identity, recipients, a threshold, then Open or Encrypt. The file chooser is an icon key with the native input at `opacity: 0, position: absolute` behind it; left visible, Chromium's own 'Choose File' button drew on top of the `age identity` label, which an earlier capture in this branch caught and this one no longer shows.
sheets.before: no SOPS document key — sheet does not exist
sheets.after: dialog 'SOPS document': Open 75×36, Encrypt 101×36, three fields 355×34, file input opacity=0 position=absolute

sheets.title: Formats on a phone — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: The same header, the same added key, in a real touch context. The panel itself is unchanged by this work; what changed is that one more key is there and it leads somewhere.

sheets.title: The sheet on a phone — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Before, nothing opens. After, the sheet fills the width. Its editor carries the 16px font floor that keeps iOS from zooming a focused control and never zooming back; `verify:mobile` measures that rather than trusting this picture.
sheets.after: sheet at full width, editor font-size 16px
